newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST-Small export-led rise in S.African 4Q GDP.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Small export-led rise in S.African 4Q GDP.

text.p: Fourth quarter South African GDP growth figures are expected to show a small increase, helped by a strong agricultural sector and a healthier export performance in the manufacturing sector, analysts said.

The consensus forecast of economists polled by Reuters was for a seasonally adjusted, annualised, quarter-on-quarter rise of 3.3 percent from 3.2 percent in the previous quarter with a range of between 2.9 percent and 3.5 percent.

Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals gave an inidication of what to expect when he told a meeting of financial market players this week that he expected a small increase in the quarterly growth rate, helped by an export-led recovery in the manufacturing sector.
The data is due for release at 0900 GMT on Tuesday.

"What we're beginning to see is the export boom behind the sudden depreciation of the currency - that will be the main boost other than the agricultural sector," according to ABN Amro economist Anastasia Gekis.
"Really it will be between agriculture and manufacturing that will provide most of the boost," said ING Barings economist Hania Farhan.

Rand Merchant Bank economist Julia Roy saw a slowdown in fixed investment government expenditure from the previous quarter but said the trade contribution should have improved, pointing to a better balance of payments situation.
Stals said recently that the currrent account of the balance of payments was improving strongly and that the 1996 current account deficit would be well below the 1995 level of 10 billion rand.

The consensus forecast of analysts polled for January trade data, which is due at 0800 GMT on Tuesday, was for a 760 million rand trade surplus, up from 378 million in November, although commentators cautioned the monthly figure was notoriously volatile.
